## 4. Proposals

A proposal is filed in the campaign's repository under `crustify/evolution/<slug>/`, as its
`PROPOSAL.md`. It states:

- the signal and its evidence, with the runs, findings and commits it cites;
- the goal it serves, by name, and the fitness measure of that goal it expects to move;
- its destination;
- the change, or the patch;
- how it was validated;
- the row the record takes when the change lands, as [`evolution-record`](record/SKILL.md) describes;
- its review's verdict; and
- its status: `open`; `deferred`, with what it waits for; `landed`, with the commit it
  landed as; `declined`, with why; or `superseded`, with the proposal that replaces it.

The campaign keeps an index of its proposals, `crustify/evolution/INDEX.md`, one row per
proposal: its slug, its signal in a line, its status, the runs that met the signal, and the
row of the record it matches, if any. The index has one writer per campaign, so that two
runs never write a row at once. It is written as each batch's proposals land, and holds
every proposal of the campaign before a wave launches.

A signal is filed once while its proposal waits. Before a run files a proposal, it reads the

PROPOSAL.md
# `CClosure::failed()` reads the panic slot an invocation holds mutably

Status: `landed`, as ffibox `a2cef17` on `devel`: `failed()` reads an atomic `panicked` flag, set after the slot's one store, and `invoke_scoped` holds no reference to the slot across the closure's call. The fix also closes a data race the defect hid: a `Send` closure invoked on a C worker thread while another callback asks `failed()`. Both cases are tests that fail under Miri on the old code and pass under Stacked and Tree Borrows.

## Signal

A tool that reports what its source contradicts: a safe method of ffibox whose `SAFETY`
comment assumes a state safe code can break.

## Evidence

Found by the ffibox docs audit of 2026-11-12, at ffibox `ca1ff67` (`devel`):

- `CClosure::failed()` is safe and takes `&self`. It reads the panic slot through
  `panicked()` (`src/callback.rs:268–274`), whose `SAFETY` comment assumes no invocation is
  running. `Debug` (`:308`) calls it too.
- `invoke_scoped` (`:333`) holds a `&mut` to that slot across the closure's call (`:340`)
  and writes it at `:343` when the closure panics.
- A closure that reaches its own `CClosure` (leaked to `'static`, through a thread-local
  `&dyn Fn`) calls `failed()` mid-invocation, then panics. `cargo +nightly miri run`
  reports undefined behaviour at `callback.rs:343` under Stacked Borrows; it passes under
  Tree Borrows. Reproducer: the session scratchpad's `closure-reentry/src/main.rs`, safe
  code but for the one C call.

No campaign code calls `failed()`; `basics.rs`'s one `CClosure` is in a test.

## Destination

ffibox: `src/callback.rs`, with the reproducer as a Miri test.

## Change

Do not hold the `&mut` to the slot across the call: take it only after the call returns, to
store the payload; or have `failed()` refuse while an invocation runs.

## Validation

ffibox's suite, and the reproducer as a test passing under Miri with Stacked Borrows.

# Evolution record

The record of what [`evolution`](../SKILL.md) landed, and what evolution learns from it.

## 1. Record

Every change that lands is recorded in Crustify's own repository, in
[`EVOLUTION.md`](../../../../EVOLUTION.md), whatever component it changed, so that a later
campaign can tell whether it held. A row gives the campaign and proposal the change came
from, the component and commit it landed as, the signal it answered, its recurrence signal
and its status, with a change that weakens a check marked so in its status. A change no
proposal filed names its campaign and `no proposal` in its place, with where it came from.
A proposal that lands several changes takes a row for each.

A change's row is drafted in its proposal, so that the review reads it. The record's writer
copies the row into the record when the change lands. An evolution branch never edits
`EVOLUTION.md`, so that two changes awaiting review never conflict there, and the record
has one writer per campaign. The record holds every change landed since it began, on
2026-11-12; what landed before is not recorded.

The recurrence signal is what a campaign would observe if the issue were back, in what a
campaign produces anyway: a review finding of a category, a run that fails for a cause, a
tool's error, a correction the user repeats. A change whose regression test checks all of
it has `test` in its place and is not watched. One with no signal a campaign could observe
has `none`, with why, and is not watched either.

A watched change is:

- `watched` from its landing;
- `recurred` once its signal is met again, with the evidence, which opens a proposal that
  cites the row: the change was wrong or partial, or the validation and review that passed
  it were; and
- `confirmed` once a campaign other than the one it came from has ended, having exercised
  it, without the signal.

# ffibox has no C half for a function without context that Rust calls on other threads

Status: `open`.

## Signal

A representation ffibox cannot express, hand-written in a campaign: the C half of a callback
whose C type has no context argument, which Rust calls later, on a thread other than the one
that received it. ffibox's own source waits for this need: `CFn`'s comment
`TODO(CFn threads): a C function that the C API lets Rust call from other threads, once a
campaign needs it` (`src/callback.rs`, at ffibox `568bcb5`).

## Evidence

`wave-226/batch-3/run-1`, the port of `src/util/thread.c`'s thread-local storage (libgit2).
`git_tlsdata_init(git_tlsdata_key *key, void (*destroy_fn)(void *))` hands the port a
destructor, which the port's registry keeps with the key and calls on each thread's value at
that thread's exit, on that thread. The C type, `void (*)(void *)`, has no context argument:
its one argument is the value, which the destructor frees (`errors.c`'s `threadstate_free`,
`oid.c`'s `thread_str_free`). `CFn<'a, P, CTX>` takes a context and is neither `Send` nor
`Sync`, so the registry, a `static Mutex`, cannot hold one, nor can a thread other than the
one that built it call it. The batch hand-wrote the C half in `thread.rs`'s `ffi_import`:
`CDestructor(unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void))`, `Copy`, with an `unsafe fn new` whose
contract states which values the function may be called with, on which threads and for how
long, and a safe `destroy` called only with a value C stored under the same key.

## Goal

ffibox's G5 (foreign patterns as Rust patterns) and G12 (unsafe encapsulated, obligations
local): its fitness measure, the hand-written representations campaigns keep beside
ffibox's primitives, falls by one per such callback.

## Destination

ffibox: `src/callback.rs` and `docs/outbound.md`'s "C hands Rust a callback".

## Change

A `CFn` without context, or `CFn`'s `TODO(CFn threads)` resolved: a C function of type `P`
with no context argument, `Copy`, `Send` and `Sync`, built through an `unsafe` constructor
whose contract names the threads and the time the function may be called for, and called
through an `unsafe fn call` as `CFn::call` is. Where the function's argument is a value it
frees, as here, the caller pairs the value with it, as binding-symbols' rule on a context
reached through an argument has it, so the call stays `unsafe` or behind the binding's own
pairing.

## Validation

Not made. Its validation: ffibox's suite and a test that calls one from a thread other than
the one that built it, under Miri and TSan; then `thread.rs`'s `CDestructor` rewritten over
it, its tests unchanged.

# ffibox has no C half for a function without context that Rust calls on other threads

Status: `open`.

## Signal

A representation ffibox cannot express, hand-written in a campaign: the C half of a callback
whose C type has no context argument, which Rust calls later, on a thread other than the one
that received it. ffibox's own source waits for this need: `CFn`'s comment
`TODO(CFn threads): a C function that the C API lets Rust call from other threads, once a
campaign needs it` (`src/callback.rs`, at ffibox `568bcb5`).

## Evidence

`wave-226/batch-3/run-1`, the port of `src/util/thread.c`'s thread-local storage (libgit2).
`git_tlsdata_init(git_tlsdata_key *key, void (*destroy_fn)(void *))` hands the port a
destructor, which the port's registry keeps with the key and calls on each thread's value at
that thread's exit, on that thread. The C type, `void (*)(void *)`, has no context argument:
its one argument is the value, which the destructor frees (`errors.c`'s `threadstate_free`,
`oid.c`'s `thread_str_free`). `CFn<'a, P, CTX>` takes a context and is neither `Send` nor
`Sync`, so the registry, a `static Mutex`, cannot hold one, nor can a thread other than the
one that built it call it. The batch hand-wrote the C half in `thread.rs`'s `ffi_import`:
`CDestructor(unsafe extern "C" fn(*mut c_void))`, `Copy`, with an `unsafe fn new` whose
contract states which values the function may be called with, on which threads and for how
long, and a safe `destroy` called only with a value C stored under the same key.

## Goal

ffibox's G5 (foreign patterns as Rust patterns) and G12 (unsafe encapsulated, obligations
local): its fitness measure, the hand-written representations campaigns keep beside
ffibox's primitives, falls by one per such callback.

## Destination

ffibox: `src/callback.rs` and `docs/outbound.md`'s "C hands Rust a callback".

## Change

A `CFn` without context, or `CFn`'s `TODO(CFn threads)` resolved: a C function of type `P`
with no context argument, `Copy`, `Send` and `Sync`, built through an `unsafe` constructor
whose contract names the threads and the time the function may be called for, and called
through an `unsafe fn call` as `CFn::call` is. Where the function's argument is a value it
frees, as here, the caller pairs the value with it, as binding-symbols' rule on a context
reached through an argument has it, so the call stays `unsafe` or behind the binding's own
pairing.

## Validation

Not made. Its validation: ffibox's suite and a test that calls one from a thread other than
the one that built it, under Miri and TSan; then `thread.rs`'s `CDestructor` rewritten over
it, its tests unchanged.

## Review

Not reviewed yet.

## Legend

- `module` / `wave` / `batch` — the batch's place in `schedule.json`: its wave's module and
  the wave and batch indices
- `objective` — `wrap` or `port`; `pass` — `first` for a translation batch, `review` for a
  review batch; `Σ first` / `Σ review` total each pass apart
- `types` / `symbols` / `fields` — the batch's scheduled units (callbacks count as
  symbols) and its types' assigned field accessors; a review row counts what it reviewed
- `$` / `tokens` / `wall` — the agent's computed cost (API-equivalent under
  subscription), its tokens in millions as `crustify usage` reports them, and its elapsed
  time, C rebuild included; `$/<unit>` divides `$` by the row's units
- `+LoC` — the landing's Rust insertions/deletions; `loc` — its `.rs` insertions
- `cov (C/Rust)` — line coverage after the landing, all test workloads in one run: C over
  the link unit's TUs, Rust over non-test sources; a `Σ` cell is the pass's last landing
- `+UB safe tests` … `+unit tests` — the tests the landing added, with its C/Rust coverage
  change in pp
- `+lifecycle` … `+misc`, `total` — the reports a review batch filed, by kind
- safety audit columns — the Safety audit's metrics, as a landing changed them
- API stability columns — the landing's items by how `ffimap api` classifies their consumer-facing API against its base: `kept`, `extended`, `changed`, `removed`, `new`, and `→Replaces` for the anchors a port moved; `unattributed` the crate's public items no anchor reaches, by module; `reasons` the changed and removed items with the reason the batch recorded

  `module wall` — first launch to final gate; `Σ recorded agents` leaves the assistant

  running it alone; `Total tests` — all four, whose coverage is one joint run's union,
  never the sum
- `total`, `ported` and `wrapped` types and symbols — the scheduled public-API units, and

# Counter schema

The counters ffimap reports: what each one holds, how a record is shaped, and
how a report is built from them. Every counter is determined from declarations
and single expression nodes -- no value is followed, no cast chain is composed,
and no dataflow is performed.

What each counter is decided FROM, and how a scan runs, is
[`analysis.md`](analysis.md); the ffibox vocabulary the `<trait>` and
`<primitive>` arms are generated from is [`ffibox.md`](ffibox.md).

## 1. The counters

Each row below is one counter, named by its dotted path into the document's
`counts`. A `{a,b}` is a split the counter carries: `raw_ptr.field.{pub,priv}`
is two leaves, and every row's leaves are integers. Each partition also carries
a `total`, derived from its children unless the driver emits it, so
`raw_ptr.field.total` exists and `raw_ptr.field.pub + raw_ptr.field.priv`
equals it; the `of_which` rows are shares of the row above them and are never
summed ([2.1](#21-partitions-and-shares)).

The counters are the whole of the document's `counts`. There is no second,
flat counter block beside them, and no prose rendering of them: a reader who
wants a rate divides the leaves it names.

Across the tree, `unsafe` and `safe` are the safety of the *function* the
position or site is in, `pub` and `priv` whether a consumer of the crate can
reach the item, and `void` a pointer whose pointee is erased (`*c_void`). A row
naming `ffibox`, a `<trait>` or a `<primitive>` is present only under
`--ffibox`, an `of_which.seam` row only with `--seams`, and a `region` or
`outside_regions` row only with `--regions`; each is absent rather than zero
otherwise ([2.3](#23-zero-and-absent)). A row ends with the property it bears
on, as [goals.md](goals.md) names them: safety, soundness, ergonomics or
idiomaticity.

### 1.1 `raw_ptr`

The raw pointers the crate declares in its signatures and types, and what its
bodies do with them.

- `raw_ptr.total.{safe,unsafe}.{pub,priv}` -- the denominator: every
  raw-pointer position the crate CHOSE, which is `fn_sig_arg` plus
  `fn_sig_ret` plus `field`. Emitted rather than derived, so it is not a sum of
  the families beside it ([analysis 9.2](analysis.md#92-what-raw_ptrtotal-admits)).
- `raw_ptr.fn_sig_arg.{safe,unsafe}.{pub,priv}` -- raw pointers an argument of
  a signature takes. Taking is the hazard: a safe fn that takes one lets a
  caller pass anything with no `unsafe` at the call site.
- `raw_ptr.fn_sig_arg.of_which.void.{safe,unsafe}.{pub,priv}` -- of those, the
  erased ones. Subtract the share for the typed ones.
- `raw_ptr.fn_sig_arg.of_which.seam.{safe,unsafe}.{pub,priv}` -- of those, the
  ones in a function `--seams` declared to be nothing but a conversion between
  a wrapper and its raw pointer.
- `raw_ptr.fn_sig_ret.{safe,unsafe}.{pub,priv}` -- raw pointers a signature
  returns. Returning one still forces the caller to write `unsafe` before it
  means anything, which is why it is counted apart from `fn_sig_arg`.
- `raw_ptr.fn_sig_ret.of_which.void.{safe,unsafe}.{pub,priv}` -- as above.
- `raw_ptr.fn_sig_ret.of_which.seam.{safe,unsafe}.{pub,priv}` -- as above.
- `raw_ptr.fn_sig_trait_impl.{safe,unsafe}.{pub,priv}` -- positions in a trait
  impl's method, both directions in one counter: a trait declaration fixed the
  signature, so the crate did not choose the position, and the figure would
  otherwise move with how many types a trait is implemented for
  ([analysis 9.3](analysis.md#93-positions-a-trait-fixed)).
- `raw_ptr.fn_sig_trait_impl.of_which.void.{safe,unsafe}.{pub,priv}` -- as above.
- `raw_ptr.fn_sig_trait_impl.of_which.seam.{safe,unsafe}.{pub,priv}` -- as above.
- `raw_ptr.fn_sig_trait_impl.of_which.std.{safe,unsafe}.{pub,priv}` -- of
  those, the ones a standard-library trait fixed.
- `raw_ptr.fn_sig_trait_impl.of_which.local.{safe,unsafe}.{pub,priv}` -- the
  ones a trait the crate declared itself fixed.
- `raw_ptr.fn_sig_trait_impl.of_which.ffibox.{safe,unsafe}.{pub,priv}` -- the
  ones an ffibox contract fixed, which for a crate built on the convention is
  its lifecycle strategies.
- `raw_ptr.fn_sig_trait_impl.of_which.ffibox.of_which.<trait>` -- those by
  trait, over the whole vocabulary, so a document says which contracts reach a
  raw pointer and which do not. No safety or visibility split: a trait method's
  are the declaration's ([2.5](#25-deliberate-asymmetries)).
- `raw_ptr.field.{pub,priv}` -- struct and union fields declared with a raw
  pointer. `pub` is one reachability question, the type exported AND the field
  exported, rather than two levels a reader has to combine.
- `raw_ptr.field.of_which.void.{pub,priv}` -- of those, the erased ones.
- `raw_ptr.deref.{rd,wr}` -- dereference sites in bodies, by whether the place
  is read or written. Sites, not positions, so they are outside `raw_ptr.total`.
- `raw_ptr.casted_to.std.{owner,string,borrow,slice,other}` -- a raw pointer
  converted into a standard-library shape, by the shape it became: an owner
  (`Box`, `Vec`, `Rc`, `Arc`), a string (`CStr`, `CString`, `String`), a
  borrow, a slice. `other` is a shape the table does not know, which for `std`
  is none of them ([analysis 11.3](analysis.md#113-other)).
- `raw_ptr.casted_to.ffibox.{owner,string,borrow,slice}` -- adopted into an
  ffibox primitive, by the primitive's group. There is no `other` arm: every
  primitive maps to a shape.
- `raw_ptr.casted_to.local_seam.{owner,string,borrow,slice,other}` -- converted
  through a function `--seams` named, by the seam's return type. `other` is a
  seam returning a bespoke handle.
- `raw_ptr.surrendered.std.{owner,string}` -- the other direction: a value
  Rust owns turned into a raw pointer by a standard-library call, such as
  `Box::into_raw` or `CString::into_raw`, by the shape it had. What C is then
  trusted to give back to the allocator that made it (soundness).
- `raw_ptr.surrendered.ffibox.<shape>` -- the same through an ffibox
  primitive's `into_raw`, `into_c` or `into_raw_parts`, by the primitive's
  shape, as `casted_to.ffibox` reads it (soundness).

### 1.2 `ty`

The types the crate defines, by what they hold and what they declare about it.

- `ty.total.{pub,priv}` -- every type the crate defines. Emitted, and the
  denominator its shares are read against.
- `ty.total.of_which.std_trait.{pub,priv}` -- of those, the types that
  implement a standard-library trait.
- `ty.total.of_which.local_trait.{pub,priv}` -- the types that implement a
  trait the crate declared itself.
- `ty.total.of_which.ffibox_trait.{pub,priv}` -- the types that implement an
  ffibox contract.
- `ty.total.of_which.no_trait.{pub,priv}` -- the residual: types that
  implement no trait at all.
- `ty.total.of_which.macro.{pub,priv}` -- the types a macro wrote, such as
  `bitflags!`'s: subtract for the hand-written ones, as for `fn.total`.
- `ty.total.of_which.{repr_c,repr_transparent}.{pub,priv}` -- the types whose
  layout is C's (`#[repr(C)]`) or exactly another type's
  (`#[repr(transparent)]`): the layouts the crate shares with C (soundness).
- `ty.total.of_which.std_impl.<trait>.{pub,priv}` -- the types that implement
  one of a fixed list of std traits a Rust consumer expects of a value, by
  trait: `Debug`, `Display`, `Error`, `Clone`, `Default`, `PartialEq`, `Eq`,
  `Hash`, `Iterator` and `From`, derived or written (idiomaticity).
- `ty.storing_raw_ptr.{pub,priv}` -- types whose fields reach a raw pointer,
  within the peel set, so these are the types that manage one themselves
  rather than delegating to `Vec` or to an ffibox owner
  ([analysis 9.1](analysis.md#91-the-peel-set)).
- `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.impl_drop.{pub,priv}` -- of those, the ones that
  implement `Drop`: they free memory Rust did not allocate.
- `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.impl_clone.{pub,priv}` -- the ones that
  implement `Clone`, where a shallow clone duplicates the pointer and, with
  `Drop`, double-frees it.
- `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.{impl_deref,impl_deref_mut}.{pub,priv}` -- the
  ones that hand out a reference derived from the pointer implicitly, at every
  call site.
- `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.impl_send_sync.{pub,priv}` -- the ones that
  assert thread safety for memory no type system checked.
- `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.has_lifetime.{pub,priv}` -- the ones that tie
  the pointer to a lifetime parameter.
- `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.ffibox.{pub,priv}` -- the ones that declare
  their lifecycle through an ffibox contract, which none of the std shares can
  see.
- `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.pub_field.{pub,priv}` -- the ones that publish
  the pointer as a public field. Not a declaration: an access the type does not
  govern.
- `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.none.{pub,priv}` -- the residual: the type
  stores a pointer and declares nothing about it, in any vocabulary.
- `ty.wrapping_unsafe_cell.{pub,priv}` -- types holding an `UnsafeCell`, the
  one way to hold a value C may write while Rust holds a shared reference to it.
- `ty.impl_block.{pub,priv}` -- inherent `impl T` blocks: the API the crate
  wrote for its own type.
- `ty.impl_block.of_which.ffibox.{layout,ref,mut,locked}.{pub,priv}` -- of
  those, the blocks on a cell and on each of its handles, which are different
  surfaces: the layout type carries the constructors, the shared handle the
  getters, the exclusive handle the setters.
- `ty.impl_block.of_which.other.{pub,priv}` -- the blocks on everything else.
- `ty.impl_trait.{pub,priv}` -- `impl Tr for T` blocks: satisfying someone
  else's shape.
- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.unsafe` -- of those, the `unsafe impl`s, which assert
  what the compiler cannot check. `TrivialClone`, which `#[derive(Clone)]`
  emits, is skipped.
- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.derived.{pub,priv}` -- the ones a `#[derive]` wrote.
  Nobody typed them, and they are most of the `std` arm.
- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.drop.{pub,priv}` -- the impls of a
  standard-library trait, by trait: `Drop`, which runs code when an object is
  released.
- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.clone.{pub,priv}` -- `Clone`, which duplicates
  one.
- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.send.{pub,priv}` -- `Send`, the claim that an
  object may move to another thread.
- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.sync.{pub,priv}` -- `Sync`, the claim that it may
  be shared between threads.
- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.ref_forming.{pub,priv}` -- `Deref`, `DerefMut`,
  `AsRef`, `AsMut`, `Borrow`, `BorrowMut`, `Index` and `IndexMut`, whose
  method returns a reference of a type the impl chose.
- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.other.{pub,priv}` -- every other std trait:
  `Debug`, `PartialEq`, `Copy` and the rest.
- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.local.{pub,priv}` -- the impls of a trait the crate
  declared itself: a shape it chose rather than adopted.
- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.ffibox.layout.{pub,priv}` -- the impls of an ffibox
  trait that states a cell's layout or how it is reached and locked: the
  layout, seam and guard groups of [ffibox.md](ffibox.md#1-the-vocabulary).
- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.ffibox.layout.of_which.<trait>.{handwritten,macro}` --
  those by trait, split by whether a generator wrote the impl rather than by
  visibility ([2.5](#25-deliberate-asymmetries)).
- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.ffibox.policy.{pub,priv}` -- the impls of a lifecycle
  policy: the allocate, release and clone groups.
- `ty.impl_trait.of_which.ffibox.policy.of_which.<trait>.{handwritten,macro}` --
  those by trait, likewise.
- `ty.generic.{pub,priv}` -- types carrying a generic parameter.
- `ty.generic.of_which.{lifetime,type}.{pub,priv}` -- of those, by kind of
  parameter. A lifetime ties the type to something it borrows; a type parameter
  makes it a family rather than one layout, so each instantiation is a separate
  question about C's bytes. A type may carry both.
- `ty.generic.of_which.storing_raw_ptr.{pub,priv}` -- the generic types that
  hold a raw pointer.
- `ty.field.ffibox.<primitive>.{pub,priv}` -- fields holding an ffibox
  primitive, by primitive: the delegation `ty.storing_raw_ptr` deliberately
  does not count as the crate's own pointer.
- `ty.ffibox.wrapper.{pub,priv}` -- the cell types: those that implement

The statics the crate defines; an `extern` block's declarations are C's.
- `static.total.{pub,priv}` -- every static the crate defines. Emitted, and the
  denominator its shares are read against.
- `static.of_which.mut.{pub,priv}` -- the `static mut`s: shared mutable state
  no borrow checks (soundness).
- `static.of_which.exported.{pub,priv}` -- the ones carrying a C symbol name,
  which C reads by that name (soundness).

The size of the crate and what its bodies do, as the denominators the rest is
read against.

  definition spans, blanks and comments excluded, so items `cfg` removed are
  not in the denominator.
- `code.loc.unsafe` -- of those, the lines inside an `unsafe` block, filtered
  the same way so the two are comparable.
- `code.unsafe_block.total` -- `unsafe` blocks, however many lines each holds.
- `code.unsafe_block.of_which.ffi_export` -- of those, the ones inside a fn

  closure inside one ([analysis 9.7](analysis.md#97-regions-and-the-c-abi-boundary)).

- `code.unsafe_block.of_which.outside_regions` -- the ones inside none, another

- `code.tests.unsafe_block` -- `unsafe` blocks in the test code.
- `code.tests.fn` -- functions in the test code, including one generated

## 2. The shape of a record
### 2.1 Partitions and shares
A partition's children are disjoint and sum to it; an `of_which` node's
children are subsets that overlap and are never summed. `nest_ptr` derives
every partition `total` bottom-up and skips `of_which` when summing, so no sum
is written by the driver and none can disagree with its parts.
`ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which` is a share family: a type may implement both
`Drop` and `Clone`, so its arms overlap and only the record itself is a
population. An `of_which` node therefore carries no `total` of its own --
summing two shares is not a quantity -- while each share keeps the total of its
own `{pub,priv}` partition. A share may refine another share, and then it nests
under it: `fn_sig_trait_impl.of_which.ffibox.of_which.<trait>` is the ffibox
positions by trait.
One child is of another unit: `as` holds the mentions of the types its parent
counts -- `ty.ffibox.wrapper` is the cell types, `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as` the
places they are named -- so it is never summed into the parent either, while
it is a record with a total of its own, which its arms partition. So is
`ty.ffibox.wrapper.fields`, the fns annotated as field accessors on those
cells.
Where a residual is wanted it is emitted as a share named for it --
`ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.none`, `ty.total.of_which.no_trait` -- rather than
left for a reader to subtract.

# API stability per C item
`ffimap api` measures a promise a C-to-Rust migration makes to its Rust
consumers: once a C item has a safe Rust API, wrapping it, porting it and its
later stages leave that API alone. It reads the crate's rustdoc JSON, finds the
Rust items that stand in for each C item through their anchors, and records
their consumer-facing surface twice: raw, as the signatures stand, and as the
**contract** a consumer may rely on whatever form a handle or an owner takes.
Two such records, one at the item's first landing and one after a later
landing, say whether the contract was kept, extended or changed. This document is what the two documents hold and every
rule behind them. The scan's counters are [`schema.md`](schema.md)'s and have
nothing to do with it.
## 1. Input
```sh
cargo +nightly-2026-10-07 rustdoc -p CRATE --lib -- -Z unstable-options --output-format json
(cd ffibox && cargo +nightly-2026-10-07 rustdoc --lib -- -Z unstable-options \
    --output-format json --document-private-items)
ffimap api extract target/doc/CRATE.json --dep ffibox/target/doc/ffibox.json > before.json
```
`--dep` gives the rustdoc JSON of a crate the measured one depends on, and is
repeatable. The contracts of handles and owners that are aliases into ffibox
(`CBox`, `CArc`, `CVal`, …) need ffibox's, since the reborrows and trait impls
those forms inherit live there; it is made with `--document-private-items`
because the bounds rustdoc synthesises for ffibox's auto-trait impls name its
private fields' types. Without it those contracts are unresolved, as section 6
describes. The measure is pure Python over the JSON. It does not use the driver, so the
crate need not build on the driver's nightly, only document on one whose JSON
format it reads.
Rustdoc's JSON is unstable: each nightly writes a `format_version`, and the
shape moves with it. `ffimap api` reads **format 61**, which
nightly-2026-10-07 (the driver's pin) and nightly-2026-10-08 emit, and refuses
any other with an error naming the version it found. Support for a new format
is added by checking the fields `src/ffimap/rustdoc.py` reads against it and
adding it to `FORMAT_VERSIONS`.
## 2. C items and their stand-ins
A C item is keyed by its anchor's `<kind>::<path>`: `fn::git_mailmap_new`,
`st::git_mailmap`, `fld::git_buf.ptr`. An anchor is a doc-comment line of its
own, exactly ``Wraps `<kind>::<path>` `` or ``Replaces `<kind>::<path>` ``,
where the path is names separated by dots and a `fld` path names a member. Every
public item of the crate that carries one is a **stand-in** of that C item, and
an item carrying several (the accessor of two members) is a stand-in of each.
What the extract reports about the anchors themselves, under `anchors`:
- `malformed`: a line that tries to be an anchor and is not one -- the verb and
  a `kind::` path inside a sentence, with a trailing period, without backticks,
  or with a path that is not names. It keys nothing.
- `unknown_kinds`: anchors whose kind is not one of the convention's (`fn`,
  `st`, `un`, `enm`, `fnp`, `tdf`, `fld`, `glb`, `mac`), counted by kind. They
  are keyed as written.
- `without_alias`: anchors on an item with no `#[doc(alias)]` naming the
  anchor's path. An item whose own name is the anchor's path is left out:
  rustdoc rejects an alias equal to its item's name, and the name already
  answers a search for it.
## 3. Locators and paths
Each stand-in is named by a **locator**, which is how one landing's record is
matched with the next's:
| item | locator |
|---|---|
| a free item | its canonical path |
| an item of an inherent impl | `Ty::name` |
| an item of a trait impl | `<Ty as Trait<Args>>::name` |
| a trait's item, a variant, a field | its owner's locator `::name` |
Lifetime names in a locator are erased to `'_`.
A **canonical path** is the path a consumer names an item by. For an item of
the crate it is the path rustdoc's `paths` table gives its definition when that
path is public, else the shortest public path it is re-exported at, the first
in order among equals. An item defined in a private module and re-exported from
its parent is named by the parent's path, and a port that moves the definition
into the parent changes nothing. An item of another crate is named by its
definition's path in the `paths` table, `ffibox::refs::CBox` for instance,
because this document does not record that crate's re-exports.
Every type in a signature is rendered by its canonical path, never by what the
source wrote, so an import or a reordering of the source gives the same bytes.
A record's `paths` lists every public path the item is reached by, from the
crate root through public modules and `pub use`, globs included. An associated
item's are its owner's paths with its name appended.
## 4. Signatures
Each stand-in's `sig` is normalised text by kind:
- **functions and methods**: `decl` holds `const`, `async`, `unsafe`, the ABI,
  generics, the receiver (`self`, `&self`, `&'a mut self`, `self: Box<Self>`),
  the parameter types and return type, and where-clauses. A method also has
  the `impl` header it is declared in, generics and trait included, and a
  trait's method has `default`, whether it has a body. Parameter names are
  left out.
- **structs, enums and unions**: `decl` holds the generics, the shape (`;`,
  `(n)`, `{}`) and `#[non_exhaustive]`. `fields` maps each public field to its
  type, and `variants` each variant to its shape and discriminant.
  `stripped` says whether rustdoc hid private fields or variants. `impls` maps
  the header of every trait impl rustdoc records for the type to its items
  (those it defines and the trait's provided ones it inherits) and its
  associated types and constants; the auto-trait impls rustdoc synthesises
  (`Send`, `Sync`, `Unpin`, `UnwindSafe`, `RefUnwindSafe`, and `Freeze` and
  `UnsafeUnpin` where the nightly records them), negative ones as `!Send`, are
  included, and blanket impls are not, since they follow from the type's other
  impls. `members` holds the items of its inherent impls that stand in for no
  C item, each with its impl header.
- **traits**: `decl` with generics, supertraits and `unsafe`; `required` and
  `provided` items, each with its declaration; `dyn_compatible`.
- **type aliases**: `decl` holds the whole target, `type = ffibox::refs::CBox<…>`.
- **constants and statics**: type and value; **associated constants and types**:
  their declaration and, in an impl, its header; **variants** and **fields**:
  their shape or type; a `macro_rules!` macro only its kind, since its body is
  not an interface.
A trait impl's methods are recorded by name only: their signatures are the
trait's, recorded where the trait is.
## 5. Handles and owners
The types a consumer reaches a C type through -- `FooRef`, `FooMut`, `FooBox`,
`FooArc`, `FooVal` and a policy type such as `FooFree` -- are not always
annotated. An unannotated public struct, enum, union or trait of the crate is
**associated** with C items by rule 1, else by rule 2, and a type alias by rule
3; `via` says which rule tied it:
1. `assoc_type`: a trait impl of the type sets an associated type to an
   anchored type, or a trait impl of an anchored type sets one to it.
   `impl CRefSeam for MailmapRef { type Cell = Mailmap; }` and
   `impl CCell for Mailmap { type Ref<'a> = MailmapRef<'a>; }` both tie
   `MailmapRef` to `st::git_mailmap`.
2. `owner`: the type's impls, or the trait's declaration, hold stand-ins; it is
   associated with their C items. A policy type whose `CDrop::c_drop` wraps
   `fn::git_mailmap_free` goes with that item.

### `libgit2/src/util/thread.c` wave 226 batch 2: the locks and threads

A `port` batch of 19 macros of `src/util/unix/pthread.h`: `mac::git_mutex` with `_init`, `_lock`,
`_unlock` and `_free`, `mac::git_cond` with `_init`, `_wait`, `_signal` and `_free`,
`mac::git_rwlock` with `_init`, `_rdlock`, `_rdunlock`, `_wrlock`, `_wrunlock` and `_free`, and
`mac::git_thread_create` and `mac::git_thread_join`. Each names a POSIX entity (`pthread_mutex_t`
and `pthread_mutex_init` and so on, with default attributes). The header keeps them for the C
that remains. Its 55 expansion sites, in `odb.c`, `pack.c`, `pack-objects.c`, `cache.c` and the
others, and the C tests, are all C and stay. So the macros need no export, and their Rust forms
are linked to no C. They are native, in a section of their own in `thread.rs`, with no unsafe
code: `Mutex<T>`, `Condvar`, `RwLock<T>` and `JoinHandle<T>`, newtypes over `std::sync`'s and
`std::thread`'s, with `MutexGuard`, `RwLockReadGuard` and `RwLockWriteGuard`, and the free
function `spawn`. Each macro is anchored on its stand-in. A type macro is on its type. An
operation is on its method: `new`, `lock`, `MutexGuard::unlock(guard)`, `wait`, `notify_one`,
`read`, `write`, and the guards' `unlock`, which are associated functions so that they hide no
method of the data. `git_thread_create` is on `spawn`, and `git_thread_join` on `JoinHandle::join`.
Each `_free` is on the type's `Drop::drop`, which is empty, the standard lock releasing nothing of
its own. No anchor the conventions gave fit an alias reached through the standard library, so the
batch filed `crustify/evolution/std-symbol-alias-stand-ins`, with Crustify `06c62a2` on its
evolution branch.

The standard forms differ from C's where libgit2's C does not rely on it, documented in the
module's `# Locks` section. A lock guards the data it holds (C's kind is a `Mutex<()>`). It
cannot fail to initialise, and `new` is a `const fn`, so a lock may be a `static`. A panic
under a lock poisons it, and a lock or wait then fails with a `PoisonError` that hands back the
guard. A guard is not `Send`, so a lock is released on the thread that took it, as POSIX
requires. The thread owns what it captures (`'static`), where C hands its thread a pointer its
caller keeps alive, and `join` returns the closure's result or its panic's payload. The
module's documentation names the configuration branches the build does not take (`GIT_WIN32`'s
`win32/thread.h`, and `!GIT_THREADS`'s `git__noop_args`), which compute the same, as
`porting-symbols` asks of a configuration-dependent macro.

Route confirmation (`dependencies.json`, libc): for `pthread_create` and `pthread_join` the
recommended `std` holds. For the lock entities (`pthread_mutex_*`, `pthread_cond_*` and
`pthread_rwlock_*`) the recommendation is `crustify-campaign`, since "the lock lives in C structs
that remaining C locks". That does not hold for these Rust forms: no lock crosses to C, so they
take `std`, the route the Standard-library equivalents section gives where no state is shared.
The shared-state case the note describes is that of a module whose layout embeds a lock that
both Rust and the remaining C take, such as `git_odb.lock`. Its batch confirms the route again,
and glibc's wrapper covers no lock yet.

Tests: 18 `unit_pub` tests (`tests/unit_pub/src/util/thread/sync.rs`) and 6 `ub_safe` tests
(`tests/ub_safe/src/util/thread/sync.rs`), modules of their own, beside 7 compile-fail cases
(a guard outliving its lock, the guard a wait returns too, a read guard outliving its lock or
written through, a lock dropped while locked, a guard sent to a thread, and a thread borrowing
its caller's data). The compile-fail cases read the same on stable and nightly. There are also
3 doctests. The unit tests carry over `test_threads_basic__exit`'s first half (the result
424242), `test_threads_basic__set_error` (four threads each set and read back their own error)
and `test_init__concurrent_init_succeeds` (ten threads, each initialising and shutting down
twenty times). They mirror `run_in_parallel`, and the pack builder's hand-off in
`notify_one_wakes_a_waiter`. No equivalence test was written: the macros alias libc's entities,
so their Rust forms translate no C logic and reach no C, and no function the raw bindings reach
runs their Rust forms. The 24 tests pass plain, under ASan+UBSan and under TSan, and under Miri
but for the two that call libgit2. Those two carry `ignore = "calls C"`, each seen to stop at
`git_libgit2_init` when run alone. The doctests pass under Miri too. BSan was not run: no test
of this batch passes a pointer between Rust and C. The module's and its 38 dependents' tests
pass plain and under ASan+UBSan, 1,153 of them, selected by test path, and 1,155 again after the
rebase onto batch 4, as do the format check, the lints, the compile-fail suite, and the
module's tests under TSan and Miri.

over HIR and typeck. Reproducible: same tree, same bytes. Needs the crate to

                        ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.borrowed.std.pub,
                        code.unsafe_call.ffi): a path that stops at an arm
                        above one validates and then reads empty, since the
                        driver emits by leaf. Line totals have no sites.

                        bindings and any other crate it reaches C through,

# The coverage report has no unit suite, which each batch merges by hand

Status: `open`.

## Signal

One procedure repeated by hand (`evolution` §2). The dashboard's `Coverage stats` table and
every batch's `+unit tests` cell read the unit suite as `lib` and `unit_pub` together, but
`crustify/scripts/coverage/report.py` reports each profile directory under `prof/` alone,
the four-suite `TOTAL` and `ALL`, and nothing that merges `lib` with `unit_pub`.

## Evidence

`wave-194/batch-0/run-1`, `wave-194/batch-1/run-1` and `wave-194/batch-2/run-1` each record
"the unit column merging `lib` and `unit_pub`" in their Notes entries. `batch-2` did it by
linking both suites' profiles into a `prof/unit/` directory of each coverage run and
running `ONLY=unit report.py …`; that directory is then one more suite for any later
`report.py` run without `ONLY`, so `ALL` would count `lib` and `unit_pub` twice in its
profile list (harmless for a union, but a trap for anything that sums).

## Destination

A campaign artifact the assistant owns: `crustify/scripts/coverage/report.py` (and the
`Coverage stats` method it serves).

## Change

Report a `unit` suite, the merge of `lib` and `unit_pub` (and `unit_priv` where a tree has
it), beside the per-binary suites, so that the dashboard's four columns are read directly.

cat > crustify/tmp/metrics.py <<'EOF'
import json,sys
def get(c,path):
    for k in path.split('.'):
        c=c[k]
    return c
def tot(c,path):
    v=get(c,path)
    if isinstance(v,dict):
        return v['total'] if 'total' in v else sum(tot(c,path+'.'+k) for k in v)
    return v
def metrics(f):
    c=json.load(open(f))['counts']
    m={}
    m['pub raw ptr']=get(c,'raw_ptr.total.safe.pub')
    m['pub void ptr']=get(c,'raw_ptr.field.of_which.void.pub')+get(c,'raw_ptr.fn_sig_arg.of_which.void.safe.pub')+get(c,'raw_ptr.fn_sig_arg.of_which.void.unsafe.pub')+get(c,'raw_ptr.fn_sig_ret.of_which.void.safe.pub')+get(c,'raw_ptr.fn_sig_ret.of_which.void.unsafe.pub')
    m['pub unsafe fn']=get(c,'fn.unsafe.pub')
    b='ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.borrowed.std'
    m['&cell']=get(c,b+'.pub')-get(c,b+'.of_which.self_in_ref_accessor.pub')-get(c,b+'.of_which.self_in_trait_impl.pub')
    m['C by value']=tot(c,'ty.ffibox.sys.as.by_val')+tot(c,'ty.ffibox.sys.as.owned.std')
    w=get(c,'ty.ffibox.sys.of_which.raw_ptr_in_sys.of_which.wrapped'); u=get(c,'ty.ffibox.sys.of_which.raw_ptr_in_sys.of_which.used')
    m['celled %']=100*w/u
    m['raw->std']=tot(c,'raw_ptr.casted_to.std')
    m['unmanaged ptr types']=tot(c,'ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.none')
    m['ptr Drop']=tot(c,'ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.impl_drop')
    m['Send/Sync']=tot(c,'ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.send')+tot(c,'ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.sync')
    m['raw deref']=tot(c,'raw_ptr.deref')
    m['FFI calls']=get(c,'code.unsafe_call.ffi')
    m['unsafe loc %']=100*get(c,'code.loc.unsafe')/tot(c,'code.loc')
    m['unsafe blocks']=tot(c,'code.unsafe_block')-get(c,'code.unsafe_block.of_which.ffi_export')
    m['_loc']=tot(c,'code.loc'); m['_tests_loc']=tot(c,'code.tests.loc')
    return m
base=metrics(sys.argv[1])
for f in sys.argv[2:]:
    t=metrics(f); print('==',f)
    for k in base:
        d=t[k]-base[k]
        print(f'{k:22} base={base[k]:.4f} tree={t[k]:.4f} delta={d:+.2f}' if isinstance(base[k],float) else f'{k:22} base={base[k]} tree={t[k]} delta={d:+d}')
EOF

cat >> crustify/artifacts/dashboard.md <<'EOF'

### `libgit2/src/util/thread.c` wave 226 batch 3: thread-local storage and `git_threads_global_init`

A `port` batch of 7 items of `thread.c`, `thread.h` and `unix/pthread.h`, waves 226 and 227 folded
into one batch: `mac::git_tlsdata_key`, `fn::git_tlsdata_init`, `fn::git_tlsdata_set`,
`fn::git_tlsdata_get`, `fn::git_tlsdata_dispose`, `fnp::git_tlsdata_init.destroy_fn` and
`fn::git_threads_global_init`, in a section of their own in `thread.rs`. The keys are native, over
the standard library alone. A registry of the live keys sits behind a `Mutex`. Each thread keeps a
table in a `thread_local!`, whose drop runs the keys' destructors as the thread exits, a thread C
started included. `TlsKey<T>` stands in for the macro: a `Copy` id, `Send` and `Sync` whatever `T`
is, since no value leaves its thread. Its methods stand in for the four functions:
`new(Option<TlsdataInitDestroyFn<T>>)`, `set(Option<T>) -> Result<Option<T>, TlsError>`, which
hands back the value it replaces undestroyed, as C's does, `get() -> Option<T>` for `T: Clone`, and
`dispose()`. `TlsdataInitDestroyFn<T>` is the destructor, a plain `fn(T)`. `TlsError` reports
`KeysExhausted`, `Disposed` and `Unavailable`. `git_threads_global_init` is `global_init()`, which
does nothing on POSIX and returns nothing, since it cannot fail.

The keys keep POSIX's behaviour wherever C's callers can see it. A value is absent until stored and
after `NULL`. A store destroys nothing. The destructor runs at a thread's exit, on the values of live
keys alone. Disposing of a key runs no destructor on any thread. The module documentation records
where they depart from it. No key is 0, and no id is reused, so a zeroed `static` and a disposed
key's copies name no key. That ends the hazard of `crustify/LESSONS.md`'s first lesson for the
read: `threadstate_get` reads its key before `git_error_global_init` and, on POSIX, reads whatever
another component keeps under key 0. A destructor that stores again while its thread exits fails,
where POSIX would run the destructors again. Live keys are bounded only by 2³² − 1 ids, not by
`PTHREAD_KEYS_MAX`. The main thread's values are destroyed at `exit` too, as std's thread-locals
are on glibc. The keys C makes hold its pointers (`CWord`) and its destructor (`CDestructor`), both
in `ffi_import`, with the `thread_local!` itself, whose expansion is unsafe code. No safe Rust
reaches them. C's destructors free the value they are given, so they reach Rust through the export
alone, never as the callable type, as `binding-symbols` has it for a function whose argument is its
context. ffibox's `CFn` takes a context and is neither `Send` nor `Sync`, so the batch filed
`crustify/evolution/ffibox-cfn-without-context-on-any-thread`.

The module's export feature, `ffi-export-src-util-thread-c`, is declared off in `Cargo.toml`. Its
gateway exports the four `git_tlsdata_*` functions for `errors.c`, `oid.c` and
`threads/tlsdata.c`, each in ffibox's `barrier`, checked against its raw binding by a constant.
`allowlist.txt` gains the four functions (`bindings.rs` `+45`, with `pthread_key_t`, which `+LoC`
leaves out). `git_threads_global_init` stays `unix/pthread.h`'s `static inline` function, whose
address `git_libgit2_init` takes, with no export, as the task message has it. `porting-symbols`'
Static inline functions section would replace its definition by a prototype and export it at the
switch. As a scratch check, not a gate, the whole workspace built with the feature on, on `plain`,
links the exports in place of `thread.c.o`, whose only definitions they are, and passes. `lib`
has 914 tests, the gateway's two among them, then `equiv` 535, `ub_safe` 808, `ub_unsafe` 148,
`unit_pub` 266, and doctests 111 and 400. In that run, libgit2's own error state is on the Rust
keys. The pointer findings of `git_tlsdata_init`, `_set` and `_get` are in the ownership store.

Route confirmation (`dependencies.json`, libc): `pthread_key_create`, `pthread_key_delete`,
`pthread_getspecific` and `pthread_setspecific` are recommended `crustify-campaign`. glibc's wrapper
covers none of them, and neither does `nix`. The port uses none of them: the keys' state stays in
Rust and crosses to C only as the pointers C stores, so the route is `std` (`thread_local!` and
`Mutex`), as the Standard-library equivalents section gives it.

Tests: 16 `unit_pub` (`tests/unit_pub/src/util/thread/tlsdata.rs`), 5 `ub_safe`
(`tests/ub_safe/src/util/thread/tlsdata.rs`) and 4 `equiv` (`tests/equiv/src/util/thread/tlsdata.rs`).
There are also 5 `unit_priv` tests: the registry's ids, and C's keys with a C destructor, in
`ffi_import`. The gateway's own 2 compile under the feature. There are 4 doctests, 1 of them
compile-fail (`E0597`). `can_set_and_get` and `threads` carry over
`tests/libgit2/threads/tlsdata.c`'s two cases. The equivalence tests compare C's POSIX keys with
`TlsKey` step by step: values, failures, and the values each side's destructor runs on at its
threads' exits. They make no C call on a disposed key, which POSIX leaves undefined: a first version
did, and C's `git_tlsdata_set` succeeded, since glibc had given the index to another test's new key.
A key past `PTHREAD_KEYS_MAX` stands for C's key that names none.

The batch's tests pass plain, under ASan+UBSan and under TSan. Under Miri they all pass but the
`equiv` ones, each seen to stop at its first C call (`ignore = "calls C"`), and the doctests pass
too. BSan was not run: no test of this batch passes a pointer that Rust reborrows. The workspace
passes on `plain`, as do the module's and its 38 dependents' tests under ASan+UBSan, 1,202 of them,
selected by test path. The format check and the lints pass with the feature off and on. Everything
was run on the base `3f7f3ab89`, and on the tree rebased onto batch 2's `8aa231a69` the lints, the
module's tests and Miri passed again. One conflict was additive: the module documentation and
`ffi_import`'s imports, where batch 2's and batch 4's `use core::fmt;` was kept once.

Coverage: `run.sh` on the rebased tree over gen5, read with `report.py` from the scratch tree's
`src/libgit2` (`C=@c` over `libcrustify.a`, Rust over the scratch `src/`). The unit column merges
`lib` and `unit_pub` through a `prof/unit/` of links (`coverage-report-unit-suite`). The pp are taken
against batch 2's row, whose tree is this base. Worklist: C `thread.c` reads 17 of 18 lines, 12 of
13 regions, 4 of 4 functions and 5 of 6 branches over the four suites, and the same under `equiv`.
The line left is `git_tlsdata_init`'s failure, which needs 1024 live keys. `thread.rs`, batches 0,
2 and 4's included, reads 412 of 419 lines, 424 of 433 regions and 105 of 105 functions. The four
zero-count lines `llvm-cov show` lists are this batch's: three arms for a value of the other kind
and a failed downcast, which the registry's kind check makes unreachable. The keys' states are each
reached: a value absent, stored, replaced or removed, the thread exiting with one, its key disposed
of elsewhere, a store during exit, and the ids running out on a local registry. The Overview's Rust
LoC moves by `code.loc.total` (`+360`) and `code.tests.loc.total` (`+936`), from the scan with the
feature on.

The safety audit scans (ffimap `50a800e`, `--ffibox --sys-crates crate::sys,pcre2_sys --regions
ffi_import,ffi_export` with the seams) are of the base `8aa231a69`, which declares no export
feature, and of this tree with `ffi-export-src-util-thread-c`. Most metrics move `+0`. `unmanaged
ptr types` is `+1`, `CDestructor`'s function pointer. `FFI calls` is `+1`, the destructor's call.
`unsafe blocks` is `+2`: that call, and the `thread_local!`'s expansion, moved into `ffi_import`
once the boundary scan listed it outside the regions. `unsafe loc %` is `-0.23` pp. Without the
feature, the deltas are the same but `unsafe loc %` (`-0.21` pp). The boundary scan's sites hold
none in the changeset. `ffimap api` over the worklist (nightly `2026-10-08`, ffibox's private rustdoc
JSON) finds the 7 items `new`. Unattributed, `thread` is new, with `TlsError`, and `sys::libgit2` is
extended by the four bindings and `pthread_key_t`; every other module is `kept`. Usage cells are the
assistant's.
EOF

Thread-local storage, native over std: a registry of live keys behind a
Mutex and a per-thread table in a thread_local!, whose drop runs the
keys' destructors at thread exit. TlsKey<T> stands in for the macro, its
new, set, get and dispose for the four functions, TlsdataInitDestroyFn<T>
(a plain fn(T)) for the destructor, and global_init for
git_threads_global_init, a no-op on POSIX that stays unix/pthread.h's
static inline function. No key is 0 and no id is reused, so a zeroed or
disposed key names none. The gateway, under the new
ffi-export-src-util-thread-c feature (off), exports git_tlsdata_* for
errors.c, oid.c and the C tests, keeping C's pointers and destructors
(CWord, CDestructor) in ffi_import. allowlist.txt gains the four
functions for its signature checks and the equivalence tests. Pointer
findings of git_tlsdata_init, _set and _get are in the ownership store.

their versions, and the workspace's `[patch]` tables, keyed by those sources, do not

2. `cargo package --offline --allow-dirty --no-verify --exclude-lockfile` packages (697
   files). Extracted under `crustify/tmp/`, the package's manifest needs an empty
   `[workspace]`, since the worktree's own encloses it, and
   `[patch.crates-io] glibc-bindings = { path = "/target/glibc-crustify" }` and
   `ffibox = { path = "/crustify-rs/ffibox" }`.
3. `CRUSTIFY_BUILD_VARIANT= cargo build --offline` there then fails in CMake: PCRE2, then
   zlib, not found. The host has neither: the bundled build finds them only through the
   side campaigns' `plain` installs, `OPENSSL_ROOT_DIR` and `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH`, the
   latter `:`-separated in the environment where `build.json`'s `-D` form takes `;`.
   With `OPENSSL_ROOT_DIR=<openssl install>` and
   `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=<openssl install>:<pcre2 install>:<zlib install>`, the package
   builds alone: cmake builds `libgit2.a` and `libcrustify_git2.a` into `OUT_DIR`.

`modules/git2/src/cli/opt.c/integration/run-1` (the switch of `src/cli/opt.c`, on
`f68ea8660`), the next packaging gate, followed steps 2 and 3 and failed to compile the
package's `lib`: two copies of ffibox, `0.1.1` by path for the crate and `0.1.0` by Git
(`40621a2`) for `glibc-bindings`, whose manifest takes ffibox by Git. The workspace patches
that Git source too (`[patch."https://github.com/crustify-rs/ffibox"]`), and step 2's
`[patch.crates-io]` does not stand for it. `opt.rs`'s gateway, which compiles from this switch
on, is the first code of the crate to pass a `glibc_bindings` `FileRef` through the crate's
own ffibox traits (`FileRef::from_ptr`, E0599 four times), so `utf8.c`'s gate could not have
met it. With the workspace's Git patch copied into the package's manifest as well, and the
lockfile the first attempt wrote removed, so that the patch applies, the graph holds one
ffibox and the package builds alone (696 files). Its `lib` tests: 829 pass and 58 fail, the
58 needing `c/tests/resources`, as at `utf8.c`'s gate. So the script copies every `[patch]`
table of the workspace, the Git sources' as well as crates.io's, and resolves with no
lockfile.

## Destination

The spec: `testing-gates`' Regressions section, with a script beside it, as `authoring`
places a procedure that must run exactly so, documented by its `--help`: it packages
without verifying, patches each unpublished dependency to the source the workspace's
`[patch]` names for it, gives the extracted package a workspace of its own, puts the
out-of-tree libraries' installs of the `plain` variant on the build system's search paths,
and builds it with no variant, in a scratch dir it removes.

content.text:
I've landed `wave-226/batch-3` as **`d3d90f565`** on `crustify/waves/wave-226`, one commit, after rebasing once under the landing lock onto batch 1 (`955c56eb7`). I've released the lock and deleted my scratch builds.

**What it does.** The four `git_tlsdata_*` functions, the key macro, the destructor's function pointer and `git_threads_global_init` are now native Rust, using only the standard library: a lock-guarded registry of live keys, plus a per-thread table in a `thread_local!` that runs each key's destructor when the thread exits.
- `TlsKey<T>` is the key; its `new`, `set`, `get` and `dispose` are the four functions.
- `TlsdataInitDestroyFn<T>` is the destructor, a plain function of the value.
- `global_init()` does nothing on POSIX and returns nothing.
- It behaves like POSIX keys wherever libgit2's C can tell. Where it differs, the module documentation says so:
  - No key is 0, and a key id is never reused. So `threadstate_get`'s read of key 0 before `git_error_global_init` (the hazard in `LESSONS.md`) now returns nothing.
  - A destructor can't store a new value while its thread exits.
  - The main thread's values are destroyed at `exit`.
- The C exports sit behind the new feature `ffi-export-src-util-thread-c`, declared off in `Cargo.toml`. Each is checked against its raw binding.

**Choices you may want to revisit.**
- **`git_threads_global_init`:** I kept it as the header's `static inline` function with no export, as your message said. `porting-symbols` would instead replace it by a prototype and export it at the switch.
- **Route for the pthread key functions:** `dependencies.json` recommends the glibc wrapper for them. That route doesn't hold: neither the wrapper nor `nix` covers them, and the port uses none of them. The route is `std`, since the keys' state stays in Rust.
- **`thread_local!` placement:** its expansion is unsafe code, so it sits in `ffi_import`, as llhttp does.
- **Dashboard merge:** the Coverage stats take the merged test counts with my percentages. No gate re-measured coverage on the merged tree.

**Gates.**
- Before the rebase, all of these passed:
  - the workspace on plain;
  - the module's and its 38 dependents' tests under ASan+UBSan, 1,202 of them;
  - my tests under TSan and Miri; the `equiv` ones stop at their first C call under Miri and are marked `ignore = "calls C"`;
  - a scratch run with the exports linked in place of C's `thread.o`, where the whole workspace passed with libgit2's own error state on the Rust keys.
- **Rerun after the rebase:**
  - formatting and lints, with the feature off and on;
  - the bindings, regenerated;
  - the whole workspace on plain (batch 1 changed the bindings and `static_fns.c`, which every binary links);
  - the module's tests under ASan+UBSan, TSan and Miri (both batches edit `thread.rs` and its test files);
  - the package gate, because I changed the raw bindings: the package (702 files) builds alone in bundled mode.
- **Not rerun after the rebase:** ASan+UBSan over the 38 dependents. Batch 1 changed only atomics and their C shims, which the TLS code doesn't touch.
- **Not run at all:**
  - BSan, since no test passes a pointer that Rust reborrows;
  - the package's own `lib` tests.

**C tests tied to the module that none of my `unit_pub` tests carries over.** Mine carry over `test_threads_tlsdata__can_set_and_get` and `__threads`. Batch 2's `unit_pub` tests already carry over `test_threads_basic__set_error`, the first half of `test_threads_basic__exit`, and `test_init__concurrent_init_succeeds`. Not carried over:
- `object/cache.c`: `fast_thread_rush`, `threadmania`
- `pack/sharing.c`: `open_two_repos`
- `pack/threadsafety.c`: `open_repo_in_multiple_threads`
- `repo/getters.c`: `retrieving_the_odb_honors_the_refcount`
- `repo/setters.c`: its two refcount cases
- `threads/atomic.c`: all 13 cases
- `threads/basic.c`: `cache`, `exit`, `set_error`
- `threads/diff.c`: `concurrent_diffs`, `with_concurrent_index_modified`
- `threads/refdb.c`: `edit_while_iterate`
- `util/init.c`: `concurrent_init_succeeds`

**Found along the way.** glibc gives a deleted key's index to the next key anyone makes. My first equivalence test called C on a disposed key, and that call reached another test's key. It could equally overwrite or delete libgit2's own error key. The tests now make no C call on a disposed key.

**Evolution.**
- I filed `ffibox-cfn-without-context-on-any-thread`: ffibox's `CFn` can't hold a context-free C destructor that Rust calls on other threads, so I hand-wrote one. ffibox's own `TODO(CFn threads)` waits for exactly this need.
- I added this run as an occurrence to three open proposals: `export-link-check`, `coverage-report-unit-suite` and `coverage-report-relative-rows`.
- I changed no skill and filed no lesson.

**Found along the way.** glibc gives a deleted key's index to the next key anyone makes. My first equivalence test called C on a disposed key, and that call reached another test's key. It could equally overwrite or delete libgit2's own error key. The tests now make no C call on a disposed key.
